doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Philadelphia's musicians and whether there is a Philadelphia sound
summary: Bryant lists Philadelphia musicians and says regional sounds no longer exist.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: What a thrill. You came from a pretty musical city, Philadelphia.
A lot of great musicians including yourself came out of there.

A lot of guys. A lot of guys, yeah. The Heath brothers, you know, Jimmy, Percy, Albert, Tootie; oh Lee Morgan, Bobby Timmons, Benny Golson. Benny and I sort of grew up together you know. And oh, McCoy Tyner, John Coltrane. It’s just full of great musicians.
Is there anything that distinguishes a musician from Philadelphia do you think?

I don’t think so. You know people say that you know, when you talk about — at least not anymore. Maybe at one time the music could be sort of like regional you know maybe, but now everything is so intertwined and it’s so easily gotten together. The world’s gotten smaller and there’s no more Philadelphia sound or anything like that. It’s said and maybe it’s true that a lot of piano players come from Pittsburgh and like that, and a lot of piano players come from Detroit, and a few come from Philadelphia. But at one time maybe we thought that we could distinguish a certain sound as being from Philadelphia or Detroit, but not anymore.
